title: Wagertech sync (Kobi/Waleed internal) - Transcript

items.topic: Figma-style layout mockups before build
items.statement: As relayed by Waleed, the client (Joyce) asked whether Jumpr could show layouts in a Figma-style tool before building. Waleed told her this does not really work with Salesforce and it is easier to update the layouts in Salesforce directly; Kobi said he told her the same.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: she's like, "Do you know with other tools when do product management there's Figma so that you can show me layouts before you code it?" And I'm… / Waleed Alasadi: "Doesn't really work with Salesforce. It's easier to just update the layouts in Salesforce kind of thing." … / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, that's… / Kobi Kunasekaran: what I told her yesterday, Nicole. Yeah.
items.note: Secondhand: client ask relayed by Waleed from a call with Joyce; client not present. Timestamp not available in allowed ranges.

items.topic: Client wants example starting points for layout feedback
items.statement: As relayed by Waleed, when Jumpr asks the client for feedback on UI layouts (what sales reps want to see), the client wants Jumpr to provide examples as starting points and to give criteria for the feedback wanted.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: last week when you guys talked about the UI layouts and you asked a question of give me feedback on what the sales reps want to see. … she's looking for us to be more strategic and provide examples as starting points versus putting it on them kind of thing. / Waleed Alasadi: And she's like,… / Waleed Alasadi: "If you want to put it on me, that's fine, but also give me criteria." So " What kind of feedback do you want?" So that's her feedback. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yes. Okay.
items.note: Secondhand from Waleed; quote shortened with ellipsis between non-adjacent words on line 31. Timestamp not available in allowed ranges.

items.topic: Build phase: fields and objects, layouts later
items.statement: Waleed described the project as still early: the team is building fields and objects, and front-end layout work usually comes later.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: … it's all like the fields we're still early usually when we come to the front end later on. / … / Waleed Alasadi: then we will be more strategic naturally. Just right now it's like we're building up fields and objects, bro. there's not much more to strategy to it.
items.note: Quote takes the relevant part of line 37 and line 46. Timestamp not available in allowed ranges.

items.topic: Subset of PRD fields built; rest held until process defined
items.statement: Kobi said fields were brought in from the client's PRD, ERD and API doc, but he added only a subset of the fields per object and kept the rest out until the process is defined; the client still found it too many fields.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: you gave me a 90page document with this an erd that has the same field and… / Kobi Kunasekaran: an API doc with the same field. brought all of that in and then now you're in too many fields where's the process? … / Kobi Kunasekaran: it was like a subset of their full list of fields that they wanted for each object because I already knew I'm not going to add fields until we define the process. So we kept those out and even then it was too much.
items.note: Timestamp not available in allowed ranges.

items.topic: Conflicting client stakeholder feedback blocks decisions
items.statement: Kobi said feedback from Emily and Lena differs from Joyce's, the client is still clarifying the process among themselves in calls, and he needs a decision to implement.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: the feedback I get from Emily and Lena are very different from what I'm getting from Joyce. and in our call they're having conversations amongst each other on clarifying the process and guys I need a decision on my end so that I can get that implemented
items.note: Timestamp not available in allowed ranges.

items.topic: Update Asana project status before tomorrow
items.statement: The Asana project plan is out of date (much POC work is done, and feedback from Friday and today is not yet in). Waleed asked to update it today ahead of tomorrow's meeting; Kobi agreed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: because a lot of the PC stuff we've already completed and then there's all these feedback from Friday and today that I haven't put into ASA but I'm working off my list right now. I'll get those added in. / Waleed Alasadi: Yeah. Yeah. / Waleed Alasadi: I think it would be helpful today we just update this ahead of tomorrow, which by the way,… / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. That's fine.
items.note: Timestamp not available in allowed ranges.

items.topic: New object added; UI cleaned up
items.statement: Kobi said another object has been added and the UI has been cleaned up quite a bit.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: No, we've added another object. we've actually cleaned up the UI quite a bit.
items.note: The new object is not named in the allowed lines.

items.topic: Layout aligned to client's updated lead/sign-up mockup
items.statement: The client (Joyce) gave an updated mockup of the lead and sign-up process; Kobi is making the layout as close as possible to it.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: she did give me an updated mockup of what she was hoping the lead and signup process could look like and I try to make it as close as possible with the layout right now. So we're working through that

items.topic: Deal rep assignment and history cleanup in progress
items.statement: The team is cleaning up deal rep assignment and its history portion; more stories are still to be written and are not yet in the plan.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we're working to clean up the deal rep assignment and the history portion for that. So there's actually a lot more stories I need to get out of here that's not reflected yet.

items.topic: Backend API is biggest risk
items.statement: With less than two weeks left, Kobi named the backend API piece as his biggest risk.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: what's your read on we have less than two weeks now left. / Kobi Kunasekaran: My biggest risk right now is the whole backend API piece.

items.topic: Bridge gap: paste Dropbox links into Salesforce
items.statement: Last week (Friday) it was decided, on Kobi's proposal, to bridge the gap for file uploads: the client uploads files to Dropbox and pastes the links (URLs) in Salesforce, with the rest handled in Salesforce.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: forth and last week we decided that we're going to just add the links the URL to bridge the gap … / Kobi Kunasekaran: So I proposed we do a bridge gap. So at least in the current process they can upload to Dropbox and paste the links in Salesforce and then everything else we can take care of in Salesforce. So we went with that as a Friday
items.note: Decision reported by Kobi; client meeting where it was made is not this doc.

items.topic: Client now wants GCP file uploads
items.statement: Yesterday the client said they want to move forward with Google Cloud (GCP) for file uploads, after the Friday bridge-gap decision. Kobi told the client there is a good chance it will not work for end of month.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: They want to do GCP as well, which they told me yesterday they want to move forward with it. / … / Kobi Kunasekaran: … and then yesterday they said they want to move forward with GCP. So I told her there's a good chance we're not going to make that work for end of month.
items.supersedes_hint: Client reverting from the Friday bridge-gap (Dropbox links) decision back to GCP uploads.

items.topic: GCP uploads as fast follow after go-live
items.statement: Kobi proposed to the client that the bridge gap (Dropbox links) be used at go-live and the GCP components be broken down and worked on after, possibly as a fast follow after go-live. Client acceptance is not stated.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: but we'll have the bridge gap and then we can start working on the GCP components after just has a chance to break down the work and then we can work towards maybe fast follow after go. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So in the interim they can still paste the links from drop offs.
items.asr_note: 'drop offs' = Dropbox [ASR?]; 'just' may be a name (Jester?) [ASR?]

items.topic: Which fields client back end can send
items.statement: API discussion is planned for tomorrow; Jumpr is still waiting for the client to confirm which fields their back end can send. The client is revamping their CMS; they seem able to send many expected fields, but this is not yet aligned.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So that one is a potential risk and then the API conversation we need to have tomorrow because we're still waiting for them to confirm… / … / Kobi Kunasekaran: what fields they're able to send from their back end. / Kobi Kunasekaran: They're also revamping their CMS right now apparently. So, it's seems like they're able to send a lot of the fields that we're expecting, but we're still not lying on that.
items.asr_note: 'not lying on that' = not aligned on that [ASR?]

items.topic: Data entry and automation cleanup ETA
items.statement: Kobi said the data entry portions are straightforward and automation cleanup will probably be done by end of this week, maybe mid next week.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: The data entry portions, all of that, it's easy stuff. we're taking care of it. We're cleaning up the automations. all of that will probably be done by end of this week, maybe mid next week.

items.topic: Re-plan next two weeks in Asana
items.statement: Waleed asked Kobi to update Asana with where things stand for the next two weeks and give the remaining work an honest assessment so they can review the timeline; Kobi agreed.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Are you able to just update Assara given … / Waleed Alasadi: where we are in the next two weeks? Just put it out and… / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Yeah.

items.topic: No separate lead object; one sign-up record with status layouts
items.statement: The client's updated mockup asked for a read-only lead object with player info and click history that creates a sign-up record on sign-up. Kobi pushed back (overhead) and proposed using the same record with page layouts by status; they agreed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: she went back to a lead object and I had to push back on this but she wanted a read only object that has the main / Kobi Kunasekaran: information related to the player, the click history underneath, and then when they click sign up, it should get created into a signup record. I'm like, that's going to be a lot of overhead for no reason when you can do the exact same thing with the same record and update the page layouts based on the status. So then we agreed
items.note: Line 104 is the 00:15:00 timestamp line between the two quoted lines. Agreement reported by Kobi.

items.topic: Rep view field set still being decided
items.statement: The rep view is to be a clean layout showing only the fields Joyce highlighted (of about 20 PRD sign-up fields); after seeing the mockup, Emily said more fields will need to be added.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: for the rep view, they basically want it to be a clean version. there's a lot of fields in there, even in the PRD, there's maybe 20 or so fields that they need to capture as part of the signup, but they don't want all of that surface here. So these are the fields that Joyce highlighted, but I think after Emily saw the mockup, she's like, there's going to be more fields that need to be added.

items.topic: Reps update sign-up status via action buttons
items.statement: Reps get a simplified layout and update the sign-up status through action buttons (flag, complete, archive, and a log sign-up button still in progress by Jester).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: basically they're trying to get this type of simplified layout for the reps and then update the status through these action buttons. / … / Waleed Alasadi: who updates the status? / Kobi Kunasekaran: it's going to be the reps for the buttons. / Waleed Alasadi: So, how are they going to do that? flag complete archive. / … / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, there's supposed to be another one for log signup. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think jester is still working on that one

items.topic: Grouped list view not possible
items.statement: The client asked for a grouped list view; Kobi said no, it is not possible. He said organizing the list view by name, operator, created date and possibly icons should be doable.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: one thing that she did ask about is if we can do these types of grouped list view and that I said no. this is not going to be possible. But organizing the list view with the name and the operator form like the created date things like that we should be able to do and even the icons we can probably do once we kind of figure out what icons they want.

items.topic: Sign-up page layout done; list views pending
items.statement: The main sign-up page layout is good to go; list views are not updated yet.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: so I haven't updated the list views yet but the main page layout is good to go.

items.topic: Layout and editability change by status
items.statement: The sign-up layout changes by status: New (the default on creation) is read-only; after log sign-up the status is In progress (lead accepted) and the layout becomes editable with checkboxes. Ops fields such as fraud status remain; extra info is hidden or read-only for reps.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So they still need those fields, but the more info we're probably going to hide for the reps or leave it and they can click into it if they want. it's just going to be read only. but the nice thing is this changes based on the status. So if I change the status to new so is the default status when a signup record gets created we hide so everything becomes read only. / … / Kobi Kunasekaran: the log signup will update it In progress will essentially make it editable for In progress just means they've accepted the lead, right? And now they're going to work on it and then now the layout changes to right like getting the checkboxes.
items.note: Built behavior shown in demo; spans lines 115 and 128.

items.topic: Path removed from sign-up layout
items.statement: The Path component was removed from the sign-up layout at the client's request because the process is not linear.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: You should add a path here. Why don't we have a path? / Kobi Kunasekaran: It's not a linear process. / Waleed Alasadi: Really? Who… / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, they wanted us to remove it. We had it in the original one.

items.topic: URL entry marks accepted via formula
items.statement: On the sign-up record, reps enter the URL; that changes the check mark to accepted, and a formula field updates the status. Only fields reps should update are editable; the rest is read-only.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: She wanted this section to be read only. and then only the information that they should update to be editable. So there's still a few more fields that need to be added here, but yeah, this section is going to be read only for the reps. This is where they put in the URL. If I'm just going to do something to put the URL and that'll change the check mark to it's accepted. there's a formula field behind the scene that also updates the status.

items.topic: Fraud review process for ops team
items.statement: Flagging a sign-up for review shows banners and sends it to the ops team to set the fraud review status (suspected, under review, confirmed). Kobi said the ops review process still needs to be figured out with the client.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But if I flag something for review, we're going to flag it. There's going to be banners and then at this point it should go to the ops team to review and update the flag fraud review status to suspected under review confirm whatever it is. I think kind of need to figure out what that process looks like for them.

items.topic: Custom click history view (LWC) deferred
items.statement: The client's desired click-history list view (all attempts) cannot be matched exactly without an LWC; Kobi plans to tell the client not to focus on it now and do it later. Waleed agreed internally. Client acceptance is not stated.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: The list view they wanted for the click history they wanted to just see all the different attempts. I can't get it exactly like this. I think I already have the time stamp. but if they wanted to see for it to look exactly like this, it's got to be an LWC and I'm going to say let's not focus on that right now and we can do that later. / Waleed Alasadi: this is perfect. push back we don't need a PC for it. Yeah. Mhm.

items.topic: Bulk deal rep assignment screen flow
items.statement: Jester built a screen flow to bulk create deal rep assignments (pick reps by profile, set active and start date) and to end them in bulk by date; he is working on showing current assignment status.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So this and then what Jester's been working on is we wanted a way to bulk create the deal rep assignments. Right now they have to do it one by one, right? Which is tedious. So we set up a screen flow. They can pick a bunch of all the reps these are the reps based on their profiles. / … / Kobi Kunasekaran: They can create active, set a start date, and then boom, it'll create the records. … he's working on figuring out a way to add the status from the current Europe assignment here. So they can see, but we can end all of them in bulk as well.

items.topic: Simplify crowded rep page; possibly split into tabs
items.statement: From yesterday's client feedback the page is too heavy; Kobi will clean it up to be closer to the sign-up page and offered to split fields into tabs. He said this will be the reps' main view.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: yeah so from yesterday's feedback even this is heavy for them. / … / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, I'm happy to split it out into different tabs if it'll make it easier. I think that might just be all they need. I think they're just overwhelmed by all these fields being here in one place. So, I'm going to work on cleaning this up a little bit to make it closer to how the signup page looks so, it's a bit simpler. but yeah, as far as reps are concerned, this is going to be their main view.
items.note: The page being shown is not named in the allowed lines (shown right after the deal rep assignment flow; likely the Deal record page).

items.topic: Reports as table view of sign-ups
items.statement: Kobi plans to create reports giving a table view of the same information, such as sign-ups for review and sign-ups in progress.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And then my plan is to also create some reports to show them a table view of the same information. these are the sign up for review, these are sign up in progress. and all of that fun stuff.

items.topic: Layouts mobile responsive; not yet tested on app
items.statement: Kobi had not yet opened the build in the Salesforce mobile app, but said the layouts are mobile responsive and nothing fully custom has been built. The work is in a partial sandbox.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Have you opened this on the Salesforce app at all? / … / Kobi Kunasekaran: No, not yet. / Kobi Kunasekaran: But this is mobile responsive. all of these layouts and everything, it is like I'm keeping that in mind. / … / Waleed Alasadi: Is this partial SB? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Partial. Yeah.

items.topic: No mobile-specific edit changes for now
items.statement: On mobile the record has no inline edit (pencil), so reps need a button (edit or complete; complete opens the screen flow for referral and proof info). Waleed said not to add anything for mobile right now.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But this one, it doesn't have the pencil. E, so we do need to have a button for them to fill in the information. / … / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think it'll just be either the edit button or the complete button. When they click complete, right now it shows up the screen flow with all the fields that they need to fill out. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So here I would put in the referral information and the proof information as well. / … / Waleed Alasadi: We don't have to change it, let's not add for mobile right now.
items.note: Internal Jumpr decision; client not present.

items.topic: Timeline risk; layouts should be last
items.statement: Waleed said he is worried about the timeline with about two weeks left, there are open questions, and layouts should be the last thing; Kobi said he may be underestimating the remaining work. Waleed asked for an honest re-plan in Asana.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: … to be honest I'm worried about the timeline right now. / … / Waleed Alasadi: … from an external read right now it seems like there's open question we should be getting into layouts as last thing right now… / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I like Okay. Maybe I'm underestimating the amount of work that's left. Yeah. Yeah. / Waleed Alasadi: because we're basically uing in two weeks … / … / Waleed Alasadi: That's why I think that's if you give it an honest thought with Basana, then we can take a look at it and.
